## Environment

Install the locked development environment:

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra dev
```

Generated Qt modules are intentionally untracked:

```bash
python scripts/build_ui.py
```

Regenerate Qt output after changing `forms/*.ui` or Qt resource files.

## Tests and checks

Run Qt tests with an offscreen platform in headless environments:

```bash
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen uv run pytest
```

PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:QT_QPA_PLATFORM = "offscreen"
uv run pytest
```

Use focused pytest, Ruff, and mypy checks for changed modules. The repository
contains pre-existing global lint and strict-mypy debt; unrelated findings are
not a reason to rewrite neighbouring interfaces.

Important focused DMA tests include:

- `tests/test_iio_scope_dma.py`;
- `tests/test_iio_mca_dma.py`;
- `tests/test_current_monitor.py`;
- `tests/test_worker_lifecycle.py`;
- `tests/test_hardware_widget_specs.py`.

## Documentation and wiki

Quarto sources live in `docs/`; rendered GitHub/Gitea wiki pages live in the
separate `wiki/` checkout. Render all documentation with:

```bash
quarto render docs
```

Do not hand-edit generated analysis output in place. Update the corresponding
`.qmd`, render it, inspect both repository diffs, and keep wiki navigation in
`Home.md` and `_Sidebar.md` synchronized with the source set.

The offline F1 reference is authored in `src/nlab/data/help/parameters.md` and
included by `docs/context_help.qmd`, so packaged help and the wiki share text.
Give each topic a stable `## Title {#topic-id}` heading. Bind Designer controls
by scoped names or programmatic widgets by attributes in `src/nlab/help/context.py`;
custom widgets can set the `nlabHelpTopic` property. Form labels follow their
field's binding. Add focused mapping and safe-input tests in
`tests/test_context_help.py`; unknown items must retain the explicit workspace
fallback rather than infer hardware behavior from a label.
The page-local `context_help_anchors.lua` filter preserves topic IDs when GFM
rendering drops custom heading identifiers, keeping related-topic links valid.

Refresh the versioned GUI screenshots after a documented widget changes:

```bash
python scripts/build_ui.py
python scripts/capture_wiki_screenshots.py
```

The hardware-independent capture script runs Qt offscreen and refreshes only
screens that contain no measurement plot, such as the connection dialog. Live
measurement images have dedicated scripts:

```bash
python scripts/capture_live_wiki_current_coincidence.py --mode current
python scripts/capture_live_wiki_current_coincidence.py \
  --mode coincidence-compare --capture-matrix
python scripts/capture_live_wiki_psd.py
python scripts/capture_live_wiki_peak_analysis.py
python scripts/capture_live_wiki_dose_calibration.py
quarto render docs
```

The live scripts configure and operate the reference hardware. Run them only
when live validation is in scope, verify the endpoint and connected sources,
and inspect their final stop/drain summaries. Never replace a live result with
generated counts just to refresh a screenshot.

The MCA/PSD/analysis helpers currently default to CH0 on
`192.168.10.135:30431`, with the CAEN Na-22 generator setup and MCA binning
128. Override their command-line settings only for another explicitly
qualified reference setup, and update the accompanying provenance text.

## Driver-derived changes

Use the maintainer-supplied PetaLinux revision as the authority for registers,
units, ranges, scan layouts, and lifecycle rules. Cite non-obvious behavior in
comments/docstrings and distinguish:

- derived from driver source;
- covered by a unit test;
- reproduced with an official libiio tool;
- validated on live hardware.

IIO sysfs values normally have already passed through kernel encoding. Apply a
scale only for explicit `*_raw` plus `*_scale` pairs when the public API needs a
physical value. Compare documented range boundaries; a symmetric get/set round
trip cannot detect double conversion.

## Live hardware discipline

- Begin with read-only `iio_info` discovery.
- Do not perform hardware writes unless live validation is in scope.
- Use a separate context per blocking/background activity.
- Stop armed cores in `finally` and close `Digitizer`.
- Test changed mappings at range boundaries, not only typical values.
- Execute walkthrough notebooks in place and verify their final cells stop
  acquisition.
- Record endpoint, firmware/IP version, channel, and independent libiio
  reproduction status.

## DMA review checklist

- Acquisition is stopped before buffer setup.
- Scan geometry is driver-advertised and validated.
- The blocking reader starts before enable.
- Only complete frames enter files/analysis.
- The core stops before drain/close.
- Reader thread joins and native buffer destruction is explicit.
- Persistent transport errors latch the session.
- File/version distinctions between Scope, legacy NDMA v1, and IIO MCA are kept.
- No code writes buffer-owned hardware gates directly.

## Builds

The reviewed release build is:

```bash
python scripts/build_pyinstaller_reviewed.py --clean
```

It emits `dist/nlab.exe` on Windows or `dist/nlab` on Linux and reports the
artifact hash. Nuitka remains available for optional standalone-directory
builds:

```bash
python scripts/build_nuitka.py
```

Tagged releases trigger Windows and Ubuntu workflows for the configured GitHub
and Gitea remotes.

## Change completion

- Preserve public IIO/controller behavior unless intentionally changed.
- Add focused tests for lifecycle, file format, settings, or analysis changes.
- Update README/wiki for user-visible behavior and the changelog for
  release-visible behavior.
- Ensure generated UI, captures, reports, and build output are not staged.
- State exactly what was tested locally, live, source-derived, or unverified.
